cardinality-F01-F30-F32.topic: How many Source, Reproductive-level and Gender descriptors a code may have

sources.source: EFSA business rule BR25 (ICT and DCF, HIGH, rejected on submission)
sources.says: One. EFSA's rule sheet gives apple juice with two sources (A039M#F01.A05YH$F01.A05YG) as a code this rule rejects.
More than one descriptor can be applied to each entry, provided they are not contradicting each other.

cardinality-F01-F30-F32.verdict: A second stated descriptor is an error (BR25). The result notes that the facet description allows several.
cardinality-F01-F30-F32.why: EFSA's checker rejects it, and the checker comes first. Only the description text disagrees.

cardinality-F03-exception.topic: The "with solid particles" exception to single Physical-state

sources.says: Only one descriptor, "apart from the specification “with solid particles”".
"With solid particles/pieces" (A06JM) is not an F03 descriptor; it is in F10 Qualitative-info.

sources.source: MTX 17.1 facet flag and guidance 2015 Table 20

cardinality-F03-exception.verdict: F03 is single with no exception; solid particles are coded under F10.
cardinality-F03-exception.why: Where a term sits is catalogue data, which wins. The description refers to a placement that no longer exists.

cardinality-F17-F18-F19.topic: How many Extent-of-cooking, Packaging-format and Packaging-material descriptors a code may have

sources.says: Several (BR25 follows the flag, which is repeatable).

sources.source: MTX 17.1 facet flag and guidance 2015 Table 20

sources.says: F17: only one, apart from "presence of burned spots-parts" (A07ND). F18: "only one descriptor ... can usually be added". F19: "only one descriptor ... may be used".

cardinality-F17-F18-F19.verdict: A second stated descriptor is a warning that quotes the description, not an error. A07ND doesn't count for F17.
cardinality-F17-F18-F19.why: EFSA's checker accepts it, so it isn't an error. The newest EFSA wording says one, so the user should know.

cardinality-F33.topic: How many Legislative-classes descriptors a code may have

sources.says: "Only one descriptor from this facet can be added to each entry." It mentions food additive classes only.
Single for each sub-list; repeatable among sub-lists.
F33 now has four sub-lists (food additives, acrylamide, microbiological criteria, veterinary drug residues).

cardinality-F33.verdict: A second descriptor in the same sub-list is a warning; descriptors from different sub-lists are fine.
cardinality-F33.why: The description predates the other three sub-lists, so "only one" most plausibly means one per legislation, as the 2015 guidance says. This is our reading, and results label it as ours.

definition-BR16.topic: What makes a stated process "less detailed than the implicit facets"

sources.source: EFSA rule sheet (2020), BR16 description and example
sources.says: A process whose ordinal code (BR_Data.csv) is lower than the implied one's. Example: A01PS#F28.A0CQZ (candied fruits, fermentation).
A stated descriptor that is an ancestor of an implied descriptor of the same facet, for base terms in a forbidden-process food group.

definition-BR16.verdict: Follow the code. EFSA's 2020 example does not fail under it (fermentation is not above "Preserving with sugars").
definition-BR16.why: What EFSA's checking tool enforces comes first.

severity-BR16.topic: How serious it is to state a process less detailed than the implied one

sources.source: EFSA rule sheet, Catalogue Browser and ICT level

severity-BR16.why: The checking tool's level comes first.
